## 2026-09-29 — Add a 'copy link' button next to the room code: trivial/haiku vs standard/sonnet
Context: card asks for a button next to the friend-room code (`src/components/MultiPlayer/FriendPlay.tsx`,
which already has a copy-code button using `copy-to-clipboard`) that copies "the join link". It reads
like a trivial one-file copy of the existing button, but no join link exists today: nothing in `src/`
reads a room code from the URL (no `useSearchParams`, no `?room=`/`?code=`). A copied link is useless
unless opening it lands the friend in `FriendPlay`'s join flow and calls `joinFriendRoom(code)` from
`MultiplayerContext`.
Decision: `standard` / `sonnet`, areas frontend+ui+multiplayer, `risk: low`, no design round. The link
consumer is bounded client logic reusing the existing `joinFriendRoom` — no relay event, payload or
Django change, so it is not multiplayer-protocol work and stays one area (frontend). Haiku was rejected
because the task needs a new URL→join branch (and the guest/not-logged-in path) that haiku's "zero
logic" row excludes.
Consequences: "share/invite link" cards for friend rooms classify standard/sonnet unless they need a
server-side change (e.g. link expiry or a new socket event), which would make them multiplayer
protocol → hard, `risk: high`.
